The investigation, published in Virology Journal, detailed the virological, age-related, and clinical characteristics of positive episodes detected between January 2021 and December 2023. The study authors highlighted that comprehensive data on respiratory viral infections in western Saudi Arabia remained limited following the coronavirus disease 2019 mitigation period, establishing a clear need to describe hospital-based detections, patient characteristics, and clinical outcomes during this post-mitigation transition. To characterize the circulating pathogens, the researchers retrospectively reviewed clinical episodes in which at least one respiratory virus was confirmed through real-time polymerase chain reaction testing of nasopharyngeal specimens, primarily utilizing a multiplex diagnostic panel. Because testing denominators detailing total negative and overall test counts were unavailable in the clinical records, the investigation evaluated the relative composition and patterns among positive cases. The team applied rigorous statistical methodologies to evaluate the data, incorporating exact tests, odds ratios with corresponding 95 percent confidence intervals, Firth logistic regression modeling, and the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to adjust for multiple hypothesis testing. The final analyzed cohort encompassed 149 real-time PCR-positive episodes occurring among 143 individual patients, though the dataset was constrained by intermittent surveillance gaps across the three-year evaluation window. Specifically, hospital clinical records were unavailable for December 2021, the nine-month span from January through September 2022, and January 2023. Among the episodes with recorded patient age, the median age was 9.0 months, with an interquartile range spanning from 3.0 to 29.0 months, while patient age was unknown or unrecorded for 32 of the episodes included in the series. Virological evaluations demonstrated that human respiratory syncytial virus was the leading pathogen, identified in 40.9 percent of the analyzed episodes, representing 61 total detections. Human rhinovirus or enterovirus was the second most prevalent viral group, documented in 34.2 percent of the episodes, making these two categories the predominant drivers of positive tests. In addition, viral co-detections involving more than one respiratory pathogen were identified in 16.8 percent of the episodes. The observed proportions of both respiratory syncytial virus and rhinovirus or enterovirus differed substantially across study years, with notable variations occurring even between identical calendar months, such as October and November, while testing sites across the medical facility also shifted over time. Age-specific analyses demonstrated that human respiratory syncytial virus detections were heavily concentrated in the youngest pediatric age brackets. Among episodes with documented patient age, 70.2 percent of all positive episodes in infants younger than 6 months were positive for human respiratory syncytial virus. This striking age concentration maintained statistical significance following Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, yielding a corrected q-value of 0.005. Furthermore, at least 33 of the 61 total respiratory syncytial virus episodes identified throughout the entire multi-year hospital series occurred within this cohort of infants under 6 months of age. The investigators also conducted detailed evaluations linking viral identity with documented clinical presentations, but observed that symptom profiles did not reliably differentiate specific pathogens. Although a range of clinical features was documented in patient medical records at the time of presentation, no statistical association between documented symptoms and specific virus detections remained statistically significant after multiple-testing correction was applied. Pre-existing medical conditions were documented in 46.3 percent of the positive episodes across the hospital cohort and showed an initial nominal divergence based on viral classification. Specifically, underlying conditions appeared less frequent among patients with human respiratory syncytial virus, yielding an unadjusted odds ratio of 0.31 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.14 to 0.64; however, this association did not reach statistical significance after adjustment, concluding with a corrected q-value of 0.057. Markers of acute clinical severity were substantial across the patient series: clinical specimens were collected while patients were admitted to an intensive care unit in 22.4 percent of episodes, and 9 of the 143 patients, representing 6.3 percent, had a recorded death at the time of data extraction. Addressing the broader public health context, the authors underscored that the absence of clinical testing denominators precludes interpreting these findings as measures of overall disease incidence or community seasonality, as the figures characterize only the proportional composition of positive detections. Nonetheless, the authors concluded that this single-center dataset provides vital local hospital reference data from the period immediately preceding infant respiratory syncytial virus immunization. They noted that accurately evaluating the future clinical and epidemiological impact of newly introduced infant immunization programs will require robust, denominator-based surveillance systems. The investigation evaluated an innovative environmental monitoring framework designed to track respiratory viruses, including influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2, across broad segments of the national population. The surveillance occurred during an exceptional respiratory virus season in which Belgium recorded the highest incidence of general practitioner visits for influenza-like illness since the COVID-19 pandemic. Substantial pressure on healthcare systems was driven primarily by concurrent epidemics of influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, while SARS-CoV-2 activity remained at comparatively low levels. Both conventional clinical reporting systems and the novel wastewater surveillance program tracked these disease dynamics simultaneously. The wastewater initiative monitored over 4.5 million inhabitants, representing approximately 38 percent of the total Belgian population, by collecting and analysing weekly samples from 30 wastewater treatment plants distributed across the country. To establish the operational validity of the environmental data, researchers compared wastewater measurements directly with figures from traditional surveillance channels. The research team computed wastewater-based epidemiological thresholds utilizing a quartile method, establishing baseline parameters to determine when viral spread reached clinically meaningful activity. Analysis confirmed that these wastewater-derived thresholds effectively monitored the circulation of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus, and SARS-CoV-2 across the target communities. The high concordance observed between wastewater metrics and laboratory-verified sentinel infections demonstrated that environmental sampling mirrored the community-level trajectory of each pathogen over the course of the season. The researchers concluded that wastewater-based monitoring provided clear added value for tracking SARS-CoV-2 compared to conventional surveillance alone, offering broad population coverage, short and consistent reporting turnaround times, and robust capabilities for pandemic preparedness. The authors also proposed several operational perspectives to refine and improve the ongoing quality of wastewater monitoring for influenza and respiratory syncytial virus. Weekly sample collection across thirty treatment plants monitored circulating respiratory pathogens throughout Belgium. Covering thirty eight percent of the population, this surveillance tracked viral presence across more than four million residents. Epidemiological thresholds determined through a quartile method allowed researchers to evaluate pathogen circulation during periods of heightened healthcare pressure. By comparing wastewater measurements directly against established surveillance systems, the study validated environmental monitoring as an effective tool for tracking community infections. High correlation between wastewater data and sentinel laboratory confirmations persisted throughout the entire winter season. The resulting findings demonstrated clear added value by providing broad population coverage alongside short and consistent reporting times. These operational strengths confirm that sewage surveillance serves as a valuable resource for pandemic preparedness during respiratory epidemics. Finally, the authors proposed several perspectives to increase the monitoring quality for both RSV and influenza in future surveillance efforts. Science及Cochrane Library,检索截止日期为2025年11月20日,并补充检索灰色文献与参考文献列表。分别针对老年人与婴儿开展随机效应Meta分析。研究采用人群特异性亚组分析与单因素Meta回归探讨异质性的潜在来源。 结果:系统评价共纳入17项研究,其中11项进入主Meta分析,另1项仅用于敏感性分析。在老年人中,合并INB为105.05美元[95%置信区间(CI):41.89–168.21美元;I2=93.2%]。在婴儿中,合并INB为5.81美元(95%CI:?35.44–47.07美元;I2=89.4%)。在欧洲亚组中,老年人合并INB为123.63美元(95%CI:41.23–206.02美元;I2=89.4%),婴儿为15.00美元(95%CI:?4.33–34.34美元;I2=43.4%)。留一法敏感性分析显示老年人合并INB较为稳健,而婴儿估计值对研究剔除较为敏感。 结论:在纳入研究所采用的阈值下,RSV疫苗接种在上市后应用场景中对老年人可能具有成本效果,而母体免疫接种的证据仍不确定。描述性结果提示,针对老年人的年龄与风险分层接种策略以及季节性母体免疫接种可能获得更高的INB估计值。研究间存在显著异质性,提示对合并估计值应谨慎解读,并强调在制定RSV疫苗接种政策时需考虑当地流行病学特征与实施条件。 主体内容总结 订阅安捷伦Seahorse XF出版物快报,了解实时细胞能量分析的各种应用实例领 取 背景:RSV是婴儿与老年人呼吸道疾病的重要病因。全球5岁以下儿童每年约有3300万例RSV相关急性下呼吸道感染、360万例住院及101400例死亡;高收入国家60岁及以上人群中,RSV每年约造成520万例病例、47万例住院和3.3万例院内死亡。世界卫生组织(WHO)已将RSV疫苗研发列为公共卫生优先事项。截至检索截止日,已有三款主动免疫RSV疫苗获批:Arexvy(RSVPreF3 OA,葛兰素史克,用于老年人)、Abrysvo(RSVPreF,辉瑞,用于老年人及母体免疫以保护婴儿)和mRESVIA(Moderna,用于老年人);长效单克隆抗体nirsevimab不属疫苗范畴,不在本研究范围内。既往系统评价虽总结了RSV疫苗接种的经济学证据,但未对单项经济学评价结果进行定量合并。2014年Crespo等提出以INB为共同结局指标开展成本效果研究Meta分析的框架,此后该框架已被多次应用,但尚未系统用于RSV疫苗接种的经济学证据合成。WHO免疫与疫苗相关实施研究咨询委员会(IVIR-AC)2021年指出,经济学评价的Meta分析可支持开展本国成本效果研究能力有限的国家进行决策。本研究旨在通过合并经济学评价的INB估计值,评估已上市RSV疫苗相较不接种的成本效果,并分别对老年人与婴儿进行分析。 方法:本综述未进行前瞻性注册,研究选择前已制定方案,方案及偏离情况见补充材料1;报告遵循PRISMA 2020,方法学设计与报告参考国际药物经济学与结果研究学会(ISPOR)成本与成本效果结局系统评价良好实践工作组报告。检索策略覆盖PubMed、Embase、Web of Science和Cochrane Library,检索词包括RSV、respiratory syncytial virus、vaccin、immuni、cost-effectiveness、cost-utility、economic evaluation、pharmacoeconomic*及ICER等;灰色文献检索涵盖INAHTA国际HTA数据库、Google Scholar、加拿大药物署(CDA-AMC)报告、WHO IRIS及美国CDC免疫实践咨询委员会(ACIP)会议幻灯片,并筛查纳入文献与相关综述的参考文献列表。纳入标准为:在上市后场景(评估时疫苗已上市且可从官方或公认价格来源获得本地疫苗价格)评价RSV疫苗成本效果或成本效用;比较接种与不接种;以英文发表。排除标准包括:仅关注疾病成本;评价假设价格或最大成本效果单价;缺乏独立疫苗组;无法推导INB;会议摘要或综述。文献筛选、数据提取与偏倚风险评估均由两名研究者独立完成,分歧经第三名研究者讨论解决。提取内容包括疫苗名称、价格、覆盖率、模型类型、时间跨度、研究视角、结局指标、模型人群规模、贴现率、国家收入水平、目标人群及资金来源等,并提取ICER、增量成本(ΔC)、增量效果(ΔE)与支付意愿(WTP)阈值;概率敏感性分析(PSA)散点图采用WebPlotDigitizer 4.4数字化。偏倚风险采用改良经济学评价偏倚(ECOBIAS)清单(22个条目)评估,以敏感性分析偏倚、错误模型偏倚和治疗效应相关偏倚三个关键条目进行总体分级:三项均为“是”为低风险,存在“部分/不清楚”为中等风险,存在“否”为高风险。主要结局为RSV疫苗接种相较不接种的INB,依据数据情况采用公式(1)或(2)计算,方差按公式(3)计算;K为WTP阈值,ΔE与ΔC为增量效果与增量成本,σ为标准差,ρ为ΔE与ΔC的相关系数;INB为正表示在给定阈值下具有成本效果,为负则表示不具有成本效果。数据准备分两种情形:情形1为报告ΔC、ΔE及其95%CI的研究,按近似正态假设由95%CI计算标准差;情形2为未报告离散度但提供PSA散点图的研究,数字化ΔC与ΔE的最小值与最大值,以PSA模拟次数为样本量参数,采用Wan等的方法估计标准差。ΔC与ΔE除以模型人群规模得到人均估计值;采用研究报告的WTP阈值计算INB,多阈值时选择同一国家所有纳入研究共有的阈值,未报告者由该国可比研究推算。成本按Turner等调整方法1统一换算为2023年美元:先按成本年汇率折算为美元,再用GDP隐含价格平减指数调整通胀,通胀率与汇率数据来自世界银行。统计分析采用DerSimonian-Laird法的随机效应Meta分析,分别针对婴儿与老年人进行;并分别开展单因素Meta回归。亚组分析按目标人群与地理区域、时间跨度、资金来源、疫苗类型联合分层。每项研究在每个特定人群合并分析中选取一个可估计方差的基线估计值;同一研究存在多个基线估计时,按以下层级标准取舍:医疗保健视角优先于社会视角;季节性接种优先于全年接种;目标人群与其他研究可比性最高者;评价不同疫苗时分别保留疫苗特异性估计值。异质性以I2统计量评估,仅在I2>25%时考虑;若某协变量使I2下降≥50%,则视为异质性的潜在来源。发表偏倚采用Egger检验与漏斗图评估,发现不对称时使用轮廓增强漏斗图探讨可能解释。采用留一法敏感性分析评估合并INB估计值的稳健性。分析使用Microsoft Excel 2021与R 4.3.3完成,P≤0.05为差异有统计学意义。 结果:共筛选2112条唯一记录,经题录与全文评估后17项研究纳入系统评价,其中12项进入定量合成(11项进入主Meta分析,1项仅用于敏感性分析),1项为灰色文献报告。17项研究均比较RSV疫苗接种与不接种,均在高收入国家开展且当地疫苗已上市:美国6项(35%)、加拿大2项(12%)、欧洲国家8项(47%)、中国香港1项(6%)。成人接种9项(53%),母体免疫保护婴儿8项(47%)。成人研究中,3项(18%)采用终生时间跨度,3项(18%)采用5年跨度,3项(18%)采用2年或3年跨度;婴儿研究中,7项(41%)时间跨度不超过1年,1项(6%)为5年。所有纳入研究均为模型化经济学评价:Markov模型最常见(10项,59%),其次为决策分析模型(4项,24%)、静态队列模型(2项,12%)和静态个体模型(1项,6%);无研究采用动态传播模型。Abrysvo在14项研究(82%)中被评价,Arexvy在6项(35%)中被评价,3项(18%)同时评价两种疫苗。疫苗价格范围为每剂170.38–305.70美元(2023年美元),美国最高、加拿大最低。季节性接种在部分研究中被评价。 结论:在纳入研究所采用的阈值下,RSV疫苗接种在上市后场景中对老年人可能具有成本效果,母体免疫接种的证据仍不确定。描述性结果提示,老年人按年龄与风险分层接种、母体免疫按季节接种可能获得更高INB。研究间异质性较大,合并估计值应谨慎解读,制定RSV疫苗接种政策时需考虑当地流行病学与实施条件。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 content_title: Flu, COVID-19 And RSV: What Virginians Need To Know Before Thanksgiving
content: Health & Fitness Flu, COVID-19 And RSV: What Virginians Need To Know Before Thanksgiving The CDC is tracking respiratory illnesses across the country as millions prepare to travel. Here's what they say to prepare for. Influenza is increasing in Virginia just as families prepare to gather for Thanksgiving, starting a season of togetherness that gives respiratory viruses plenty of opportunities to spread. Nationally, seasonal flu activity is increasing in many areas, while viruses that commonly cause colds are circulating at elevated levels, according to the latest update from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. COVID-19 activity is declining nationally, with emergency department visits low and decreasing. Still, wastewater monitoring shows moderate levels of the virus circulating nationwide, with some states reporting high levels. Find out what's happening in Across Virginiafor free with the latest updates from Patch. RSV, or respiratory syncytial virus, usually causes cold-like symptoms but can be serious for infants and older adults. Emergency department visits remain low nationally but are increasing in many areas. Wastewater readings for RSV and influenza A remain very low nationally. In Virginia, RSV and influenza A levels likewise are low, but growing. COVID-19 levels, at least according to some metrics, are high. Find out what's happening in Across Virginiafor free with the latest updates from Patch. In Virginia, current respiratory illness levels are low, as measured by the CDC’s acute respiratory illness metric, which tracks activity levels. In Washington, DC, Northern Virginia’s near neighbor, levels are very low. RSV levels in the state are also very low. Wastewater viral activity levels for RSV and influenza A are very low, but COVID-19 levels are high across the state, and very high in Washington, DC. Based on emergency department visits and estimates of how many people are infected by a single sick individual over time, the CDC gauges that RSV and influenza A outbreaks are growing in the state. COVID-19 is assessed as likely growing. Vaccines Help, But Hurry Vaccines help, too, but it takes about two weeks for full protection to begin. So if you’re planning on getting a vaccination, now is the time to do it. Getting vaccinated later can still help protect against illness during the rest of the season. This season’s flu shot targets H1N1, the influenza A subtype causing most reported flu infections so far, along with H3N2 and an influenza B strain. Early laboratory testing suggests the vaccine is a good match for most H1N1 viruses tested, according to the CDC, although it’s too early to know how much protection that will translate into during this flu season. This season’s updated COVID-19 vaccines target XFG, a descendant of the Omicron variant, according to the CDC. The formula was selected to better match circulating viruses, but the shots don’t guarantee protection against infection. Their main benefit remains reducing the risk of serious illness, hospitalization and death. RSV vaccines help prevent serious illness from respiratory syncytial virus, which usually causes cold-like symptoms but can lead to pneumonia and hospitalization. The CDC recommends vaccination for adults 75 and older and those ages 50 to 74 at increased risk. Unlike flu shots, RSV vaccination isn’t currently annual: People who have already received a dose shouldn’t get another at this time. Check which flu, COVID-19 and RSV immunizations are recommended for your age and health. A pharmacist or other health care provider can help sort that out, and getting vaccinated often doesn’t require a separate doctor’s visit. Pharmacies, including CVS and Walgreens, offer the shots to eligible patients, generally at no cost with most insurance. Don’t Show Up Sick Nobody wants to miss Thanksgiving dinner, but showing up sick can send more than leftovers home with the family. The CDC recommends staying home and away from others until symptoms have been improving overall and you’ve been fever-free without fever-reducing medicine for at least 24 hours. For the next five days, take extra precautions because you may still be contagious. Hosts can help by bringing in fresh air. Open windows when practical, run a portable HEPA air cleaner or take some of the gathering outside if the weather cooperates. Testing before getting together can add protection, especially when visiting someone at higher risk. But a negative rapid test isn’t an all-clear if you’re coughing, feverish or otherwise feeling sick. A well-fitting N95 or KN95 mask can also reduce risk in crowded indoor spaces, during travel or around vulnerable relatives. The familiar advice still applies. Wash your hands, cover coughs and sneezes, and clean frequently touched surfaces. Get more local news delivered straight to your inbox. Sign up for free Patch newsletters and alerts

content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, November 18, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Marketed RSV Vaccines Prove Cost-Effective for Older Adults but Inconclusive for Infants by November 16, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Marketed RSV Vaccines Prove Cost-Effective for Older Adults but Inconclusive for Infants Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A comprehensive systematic review and meta-analysis published in Infectious Diseases of Poverty demonstrates that newly marketed respiratory syncytial virus vaccines may be cost-effective for older adults, whereas economic evidence for maternal vaccination protecting infants remains inconclusive. Conducted by researchers Mengyao Mu, Yang Deng, Zhanwei Du, and Yi Zhao, the investigation synthesized incremental net benefit metrics from economic evaluations published through late 2025. Rather than modeling hypothetical price thresholds or maximum cost-effective benchmarks, the authors restricted inclusion exclusively to post-marketing environments where vaccines possessed established commercial prices from official sources. By synthesizing findings across independently developed economic models, the investigators sought to provide standardized economic evidence to inform national immunization advisory bodies and healthcare resource allocators. The quantitative synthesis demonstrated a statistically significant positive pooled net benefit for older adult vaccination, contrasting with a statistically non-significant, highly sensitive economic profile observed across maternal immunization models designed to safeguard newborns against lower respiratory infections. The impetus for evaluating these vaccines stems from the substantial global disease burden exerted by respiratory syncytial virus across vulnerable age groups. Epidemiological data indicate the pathogen causes approximately 33.0 million acute lower respiratory infection episodes, 3.6 million hospital admissions, and 101,400 attributable deaths annually among children under five years of age worldwide. Among individuals aged 60 years and older within high-income nations, the virus accounts for roughly 5.2 million clinical cases, 470,000 hospitalizations, and 33,000 in-hospital deaths each year. Consequently, the World Health Organization designated respiratory syncytial virus vaccine development as an urgent public health priority. By the study search cutoff, three active vaccines had gained regulatory approval: Arexvy by GlaxoSmithKline for older adults, Abrysvo by Pfizer for older adults and maternal immunization, and mRESVIA by Moderna for older adults. Monoclonal antibodies such as nirsevimab were excluded from the review because they provide passive infant prophylaxis rather than active immunization. To address methodological challenges that previously prevented quantitative pooling of economic evaluations, the authors implemented the incremental net benefit framework introduced by Crespo and colleagues in 2014. Previous reviews summarized economic evaluations across diverse settings but avoided statistical pooling. Directly pooling incremental cost-effectiveness ratios is flawed because ratios are volatile when incremental clinical gains approach zero, generating distorted or uninterpretable values. In contrast, calculating incremental net benefit projects cost-effectiveness onto a linear monetary scale by multiplying willingness-to-pay thresholds by incremental health effects and subtracting incremental expenditures. This approach enables valid statistical synthesis across divergent healthcare jurisdictions while preserving interpretability. As noted by the World Health Organization Immunization and Vaccine-Related Implementation Research Advisory Committee in 2021, meta-analyses of economic evaluations provide critical support for health ministries with limited capacity to conduct domestic modeling, establishing standardized benchmarks for evaluating whether novel vaccines deliver acceptable value relative to their acquisition costs. Discover more vaccine Vaccines vaccines Find Vaccines Vaccine The review followed Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses 2020 guidelines and incorporated principles from the International Society for Pharmacoeconomics and Outcomes Research Good Practices Task Force Report. The research team searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library through November 20, 2025, deploying controlled vocabulary and text keywords for respiratory syncytial virus, vaccination, and economic evaluations. Additional gray literature searches covered the International Network of Agencies for Health Technology Assessment, Google Scholar, Canada’s Drug Agency, the World Health Organization repository, and United States Centers for Disease Control and Prevention advisory committee presentations. Two independent reviewers conducted screening, resolving disagreements with a third investigator. From 2,112 unique records screened, seventeen studies met inclusion criteria: published in English, assessing marketed vaccines with official pricing against no vaccination, and providing data to derive incremental net benefits. Studies evaluating hypothetical pricing, maximum cost-effective thresholds, or lacking standalone vaccine arms were excluded. All seventeen included economic evaluations were model-based investigations conducted in high-income settings: six in the United States, two in Canada, eight in Europe, and one in Hong Kong. Nine evaluated adult vaccination, while eight evaluated maternal immunization protecting infants. Regarding modeling frameworks, ten studies utilized Markov models, four implemented decision-analytic models, two used static cohort models, and one applied a static individual-based model, with dynamic transmission models absent. Abrysvo was examined in fourteen studies and Arexvy in six, with three evaluating both vaccines. Reported vaccine prices ranged from USD 170.38 to USD 305.70 per dose in 2023 currency, peaking in the United States and lowest in Canada. Twelve studies adopted societal perspectives, twelve evaluated healthcare payer perspectives, and seven reported both. Ten studies received manufacturer funding, while seven relied on public, non-industry, or internal support. Methodological quality appraisal via the 22-item Economic Evaluation Bias checklist categorized twelve studies as low risk of bias, four as moderate risk, and one as high risk. To synthesize disparate economic data, the authors converted all financial values into 2023 United States dollars using local exchange rates and World Bank GDP implicit price deflators. Incremental net benefits and variances were calculated from reported confidence intervals or digitized from probabilistic sensitivity analysis scatter plots using WebPlotDigitizer and Wan’s formula. DerSimonian and Laird random-effects meta-analyses were executed separately for older adult and infant cohorts using R and Microsoft Excel. To avoid double-counting within studies reporting multiple scenarios, the researchers applied a strict hierarchy: selecting healthcare over societal perspectives, seasonal over year-round administration, and maximally comparable demographic groups. Statistical heterogeneity was quantified using the I-squared metric, where values over 25 percent indicated heterogeneity and reductions of 50 percent or more identified potential explanatory variables during univariable meta-regressions. Egger’s tests and contour-enhanced funnel plots evaluated publication bias, while leave-one-out sensitivity analyses tested the robustness of the pooled estimates. The primary meta-analysis established that older adult vaccination was cost-effective at study-specific thresholds, yielding a pooled incremental net benefit of USD 105.05 (95% CI: 41.89 to 168.21; I2 = 93.2%) when retaining the Hutton Abrysvo estimate, and USD 105.81 (95% CI: 41.08 to 170.53; I2 = 93.4%) with Hutton Arexvy. Leave-one-out analyses confirmed older adult benefits remained positive and statistically significant throughout. Adding Singer’s evaluation of adults aged 50 to 59 with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease caused negligible change. Conversely, maternal vaccination yielded a pooled incremental net benefit of USD 5.81 (95% CI: -35.44 to 47.07; I2 = 89.4%), failing to achieve statistical significance. Infant estimates displayed marked sensitivity: excluding Averin or Álvarez Aldean turned the pooled benefit negative, whereas omitting Wang produced a statistically significant positive benefit of USD 23.98 (95% CI: 0.45 to 47.51) and lowered I2 to 60.5%. Egger’s tests indicated funnel asymmetry in older adult models (P = 0.014 and P = 0.015), whereas infant models showed none (P = 0.953). Subgroup analyses and univariable meta-regressions highlighted substantial variation across geographic regions, analytical horizons, funding sources, and vaccine brands. Regionally, European older adult evaluations demonstrated a statistically significant pooled incremental net benefit of USD 123.63 (95% CI: 41.23 to 206.02; I2 = 89.4%), whereas United States models yielded an imprecise, non-significant USD 169.33 (95% CI: -208.03 to 546.69; I2 = 91.3%). Among infant studies, the European subgroup yielded USD 15.00 (95% CI: -4.33 to 34.34) with markedly lower heterogeneity (I2 = 43.4%), where meta-regression confirmed geographic region as an explanatory covariate. Analytical time horizon also influenced outcomes: older adult studies evaluating horizons of five years or longer yielded a significant pooled benefit of USD 151.33 (95% CI: 65.90 to 236.76; I2 = 88.9%). Manufacturer-funded adult studies, which consistently utilized longer horizons, reported USD 151.33, while non-manufacturer infant studies produced a negative pooled benefit of USD -38.63 compared with positive USD 34.49 for industry-funded infant evaluations. By vaccine brand, older adult Abrysvo evaluations were statistically significant at USD 74.14, whereas Arexvy yielded a non-significant USD 154.69. Descriptive findings extracted across individual models revealed that targeting specific risk groups and tailoring vaccination timing improved cost-effectiveness. In older adults, Hutton and colleagues observed that incremental net benefit increased as the minimum eligibility age rose from 60 to 75 years, before declining slightly at 80 years. In Canadian modeling by Rudd, broad vaccination targeting both average-risk and high-risk adults generated distinctly negative net benefits, whereas strategies targeting high-risk older adults produced favorable economic returns. Tuite similarly demonstrated that targeting high-risk adults aged 70 and older was superior to general age-based vaccination. For maternal vaccination, three studies directly comparing seasonal and year-round strategies—Averin, Li, and Wang—found that seasonal administration consistently produced higher incremental net benefits. Averin noted that wider vaccination windows prevented more cases but diminished economic value. Furthermore, Nguyen found maternal vaccination was cost-saving for infants born between October and December, cost-effective for January births, but not cost-effective for February births. Interpreting these findings requires accounting for biological dynamics, methodological discrepancies, and study limitations. Biologically, adult vaccination induces active immunity capable of generating multi-year health benefits and healthcare cost offsets, whereas maternal vaccination provides passive protection via maternal antibodies that wane during infancy, explaining why time horizons heavily affect adult economic models. Divergent results between United States models by Hutton and La reflected differing assumptions regarding hospitalization rates, protection duration, and sequelae, while Hong Kong models reflected lower healthcare costs yielding smaller absolute cost offsets. Crucially, substantial between-study heterogeneity and the exclusive focus on high-income settings limit generalizability to lower-income regions with differing disease burden and healthcare financing. Additionally, the exclusion of monoclonal antibodies like nirsevimab confines conclusions to maternal vaccines rather than all infant interventions, and the absence of prospective protocol registration may elevate risk of reporting bias. Consequently, the authors conclude that policymakers must interpret pooled net benefit estimates cautiously, tailoring vaccination programs to local epidemiology, healthcare costs, and implementation conditions. The investigation evaluated an innovative environmental monitoring framework designed to track respiratory viruses, including influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2, across broad segments of the national population. The surveillance occurred during an exceptional respiratory virus season in which Belgium recorded the highest incidence of general practitioner visits for influenza-like illness since the COVID-19 pandemic. Substantial pressure on healthcare systems was driven primarily by concurrent epidemics of influenza and respiratory syncytial virus, while SARS-CoV-2 activity remained at comparatively low levels. Both conventional clinical reporting systems and the novel wastewater surveillance program tracked these disease dynamics simultaneously. The wastewater initiative monitored over 4.5 million inhabitants, representing approximately 38 percent of the total Belgian population, by collecting and analysing weekly samples from 30 wastewater treatment plants distributed across the country. Discover more Research assistant services Postdoc opportunities Research report templates Learn Engineering Track Biotech To establish the operational validity of the environmental data, researchers compared wastewater measurements directly with figures from traditional surveillance channels. The research team computed wastewater-based epidemiological thresholds utilizing a quartile method, establishing baseline parameters to determine when viral spread reached clinically meaningful activity. Analysis confirmed that these wastewater-derived thresholds effectively monitored the circulation of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus, and SARS-CoV-2 across the target communities. The high concordance observed between wastewater metrics and laboratory-verified sentinel infections demonstrated that environmental sampling mirrored the community-level trajectory of each pathogen over the course of the season. The researchers concluded that wastewater-based monitoring provided clear added value for tracking SARS-CoV-2 compared to conventional surveillance alone, offering broad population coverage, short and consistent reporting turnaround times, and robust capabilities for pandemic preparedness. The authors also proposed several operational perspectives to refine and improve the ongoing quality of wastewater monitoring for influenza and respiratory syncytial virus. Weekly sample collection across thirty treatment plants monitored circulating respiratory pathogens throughout Belgium. Covering thirty eight percent of the population, this surveillance tracked viral presence across more than four million residents. Epidemiological thresholds determined through a quartile method allowed researchers to evaluate pathogen circulation during periods of heightened healthcare pressure. By comparing wastewater measurements directly against established surveillance systems, the study validated environmental monitoring as an effective tool for tracking community infections. The resulting findings demonstrated clear added value by providing broad population coverage alongside short and consistent reporting times. These operational strengths confirm that sewage surveillance serves as a valuable resource for pandemic preparedness during respiratory epidemics. Finally, the authors proposed several perspectives to increase the monitoring quality for both RSV and influenza in future surveillance efforts. RSVPreF3后一个月相对于第一剂后RSV-A和RSV-B中和滴度的平均几何增长。次要结局包括移植受者与对照组相比的安全性和免疫原性评估。在接受两剂的移植受者中,第二剂后一个月针对RSV-A和RSV-B的中和滴度在数值上高于第一剂后(平均几何增长:RSV-A为1.34[95% CI:1.20,1.48][n=111],RSV-B为1.26[95% CI:1.14,1.40][n=111])。单剂在移植受者中具有免疫原性,但初始中和应答较非免疫功能受损对照组更慢且总体更低,尤其在接受麦考酚酸类药物治疗的个体中。所有组接种后RSVPreF3特异性CD4+ T细胞频率较基线升高。体液和细胞介导免疫应答在接种后12个月内持续高于基线。两剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3均耐受良好,安全性特征相似且可接受。总体而言,上述结果支持adjuvanted RSVPreF3在肾和肺移植受者中具有有利的获益-风险特征。 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)等常见呼吸道病毒对免疫功能受损个体构成显著的发病和死亡风险。此类免疫功能受损状态包括原发性免疫缺陷、长期(移植后)免疫抑制治疗、血液系统恶性肿瘤或人类免疫缺陷病毒感染等,可增加个体对迁延性和更严重RSV疾病的易感性。超过三分之一的免疫功能受损RSV感染者可发生肺炎和住院。此外,受累个体常遗留长期后遗症;一项系统综述报告,近半数感染RSV的肺移植受者出现肺功能下降。该群体还面临RSV相关移植物并发症(急性细胞排斥、移植物功能障碍或慢性肺移植物功能障碍)的高风险。RSV相关死亡率相当可观;因RSV住院的造血干细胞移植受者中,全因死亡中位率达17.5%,成人骨髓移植受者中RSV相关汇总病死率为6.0%。成人RSV疾病的治疗选择在很大程度上仍以支持治疗为主,凸显了疫苗接种等预防策略对高危群体的重要性。然而,免疫功能受损人群的疫苗应答常常减弱,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)、流感及其他疫苗中均可见此现象。在移植受者中,特定免疫抑制方案尤其是麦考酚酸类化合物是免疫原性降低的关键因素。增加疫苗剂次可能有助于改善和维持保护。基于预融合F蛋白的疫苗代表RSV预防的重大进展。RSV F蛋白作为此类疫苗的抗原靶点,在RSV-A和RSV-B两种不同亚型间高度保守,两种亚型可共同流行,且常随地点和季节变化而消长。由于RSV-A和RSV-B共享该抗原,单价F蛋白疫苗可提供跨亚型保护。此外,F蛋白的预融合形式负责大部分中和抗体活性。AS01E佐剂化RSV预融合F蛋白疫苗(adjuvanted RSVPreF3,Arexvy,GSK)可预防成人RSV-A和RSV-B亚型所致疾病。在非免疫功能受损老年人的1/2期剂量选择研究中,adjuvanted RSVPreF3单剂即可引发稳健免疫应答,两个月后第二剂未观察到额外免疫原性获益,支持该人群采用单剂基础方案。adjuvanted RSVPreF3最初在美国和欧洲获批作为单剂疫苗用于≥60岁人群及50–59岁重度RSV疾病风险增加人群。此后适应证已扩展至美国≥18岁重度RSV疾病风险增加成人(2026年3月),以及欧洲所有≥18岁成人(2026年1月)。在≥60岁人群中,一剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3在三个RSV季节内对RSV相关下呼吸道疾病的累积效力为62.9%(97.5%置信区间[CI]:46.7,74.8),近期真实世界有效性研究通过显示单剂RSV疫苗接种后RSV相关住院减少而佐证了上述发现。在伴有增加重度RSV疾病风险的慢性疾病(如肺病、心血管疾病、糖尿病)的≥60岁人群中,疫苗效力仍保持较高水平,免疫原性与无此类疾病个体相当。在伴有或不伴有此类慢性疾病的50–59岁人群及伴有类似疾病的18–49岁人群中,adjuvanted RSVPreF3对RSV-A和RSV-B中和滴度的免疫原性非劣效于≥60岁人群。该疫苗在这些年龄组中显示出可接受的安全性特征。对于免疫功能受损个体,新兴真实世界数据和免疫原性研究提示基于预融合F蛋白的RSV疫苗可减少RSV相关住院并引发免疫应答。然而,该人群中现有证据仍然有限,常合并异质性患者群体,且多为观察性研究。本研究呈现了一项多国、多中心试验(NCT05921903)的结果,该试验评估了adjuvanted RSVPreF3在≥18岁接受维持免疫抑制方案的肺或肾移植受者中,单剂或间隔30–60天两剂方案后的免疫原性、反应原性和安全性。≥50岁非免疫功能受损个体作为单剂对照。鉴于免疫功能受损个体可能存在次优免疫应答,主要研究目标为评估移植受者第二剂后免疫应答是否高于第一剂后。次要目标为描述移植受者与对照组相比的安全性和免疫原性。研究还评估了疫苗在接受含麦考酚酸方案与不含麦考酚酸方案的移植受者中的免疫原性。参与者接种后随访12个月以评估长期免疫原性和安全性。 研究共纳入两个人群:免疫功能受损个体和非免疫功能受损个体,随访至(末次)接种后12个月,跨越5至6个预定访视以评估免疫原性和安全性。免疫功能受损队列由≥18岁、移植后至少一年且接受维持治疗以预防同种异体移植物排斥的肺或肾移植受者组成。这些参与者按1:1随机接受一剂(1剂移植组,n=131)或间隔30–60天两剂(2剂移植组,n=130)adjuvanted RSVPreF3。非免疫功能受损≥50岁成人作为对照,接受一剂(非免疫功能受损组,n=125)。每组约30%的参与者(选自特定国家和临床中心)参与细胞介导免疫原性评估,并增加一次第一剂后早期访视。总计386名参与者接受至少一剂疫苗,377名(97.7%)完成研究。暴露人群中各组基线特征总体相似,但合并症因入选标准而异。1剂移植组中位年龄63.0岁,2剂移植组62.0岁,非免疫功能受损组64.0岁。1剂和2剂移植组中分别有70.2%和72.3%的参与者接受肾移植,其余为肺移植。末次移植至第一访视的中位间隔在移植组间均衡(1剂移植组:67个月[最小–最大:12–386],2剂移植组:60个月[14–450])。总体而言,59.4%的移植受者接受含麦考酚酸类化合物、皮质类固醇和钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂(和/或哺乳动物雷帕霉素靶蛋白[mTOR]抑制剂)联合方案;36.8%接受含麦考酚酸类化合物、皮质类固醇和钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂(和/或mTOR抑制剂)中任意两者联合的方案;3.8%接受含单一成分的方案。几乎所有移植受者(99.6%)接受含钙调神经磷酸酶抑制剂(和/或mTOR抑制剂)的方案;79.3%接受含皮质类固醇的方案,76.6%接受含麦考酚酸类的方案。每次访视时,各组超过80%的参与者纳入体液免疫原性符合方案集。主要描述性终点为2剂移植组第二剂后约一个月(第4访视)相对于第一剂后约一个月(第3访视)RSV-A和RSV-B中和滴度的平均几何增长(MGI)。第二剂后相对于第一剂后的MGI为RSV-A 1.34(95% CI:1.20,1.48),RSV-B 1.26(1.14,1.40),表明在移植受者中第二剂诱导的中和滴度高于第一剂(RSV-A和RSV-B符合方案集中两个时间点均有免疫原性数据的n=111)。基线时所有参与者RSV-A和RSV-B中和滴度均高于检测 cut-off(RSV-A为18估计稀释度[ED60],RSV-B为30 讨论部分指出,免疫功能受损个体面临重度RSV结局风险增加,是疫苗接种的重要优先人群。RSV疫苗在免疫功能受损个体中的免疫原性数据及真实世界有效性证据正在积累,但多数证据来自包含多样化免疫功能受损亚组的广泛异质性队列。本研究呈现了adjuvanted RSVPreF3在接受维持免疫抑制方案的肺和肾移植受者中的免疫原性、反应原性和安全性,其中76.6%接受麦考酚酸类化合物。描述性免疫原性分析显示,单剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3可提高肺和肾移植受者的体液和细胞介导免疫应答,应答持续至接种后12个月。针对RSV-A和RSV-B亚型均产生强中和抗体应答,两个亚型在各时间点应答相似,证明跨RSV亚型一致且广泛反应性的免疫特征。然而,与非免疫功能受损对照相比,移植受者单剂后通常表现出更慢的诱导和更低的RSV-A和RSV-B中和滴度。间隔1–2个月第二剂后,移植受者滴度进一步升高,与非免疫功能受损个体范围相似。该应答模式主要在接收麦考酚酸类的移植受者中观察到,其单剂后初始滴度通常低于非免疫功能受损人群,但第二剂后达到相似范围。未接受麦考酚酸类的受者单剂后RSV-A/RSV-B滴度在所有时间点与非免疫功能受损组范围相似,第二剂未导致进一步升高。上述发现与免疫抑制人群中其他疫苗(流感、SARS-CoV-2、肺炎球菌等)的既往研究一致,这些研究将麦考酚酸确定为体液免疫原性降低的强预测因素。细胞介导免疫原性在每组小部分参与者中评估;总体而言,一剂或两剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3诱导的RSVPreF3特异性CD4+ T细胞应答在所有组中至研究结束仍高于基线。在该免疫功能受损人群中观察到的稳健且持续的体液和细胞免疫应答值得关注。AS01E佐剂与强而持久的CD4+ T细胞应答及高中和滴度相关,可能有助于在免疫抑制背景下观察到该免疫原性。两种给药方案的adjuvanted RSVPreF3均耐受良好,安全性特征可接受。大多数征集性事件为轻至中度且短暂,非征集性AE在各组间总体相当。移植受者SAE报告频率高于非免疫功能受损个体;移植组最常见SAE系统器官分类为感染和侵染,最常见SAE为肺炎,与该人群对重度呼吸道感染的已知易感性一致。一例SAE被研究者评估为疫苗相关(1剂移植组胃肠炎),由于患者炎症状态、潜在混杂因素及因果关系证据不足,申办方评估该事件与研究干预无关。目前免疫功能受损人群中RSV疫苗数据有限,且 largely 反映单剂评估。现有免疫原性数据在各研究间差异较大,可能反映研究规模、设计、基础疾病和免疫抑制方案的差异。一项在免疫功能受损成人(主要为实体器官移植受者)中的小型研究显示,单剂两种RSV疫苗之一(包括adjuvanted RSVPreF3)可引发中和抗体应答,但与本研究观察相似,较非免疫功能受损人群历史数据应答降低。一项在异基因造血干细胞移植和肺移植受者中的单中心干预性队列研究也注意到,单剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3后约一个月两种情况下体液免疫应答均适度增加。另一项在肺移植受者中的单中心回顾性队列研究报告,单剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3诱导的抗体应答持续高于基线至接种后六个月。评估免疫功能受损人群中两剂RSV疫苗接种策略的临床研究显示结果不一。在一项mRNA-1345 RSV疫苗(mRESVIA,Moderna)在肝、肾和肺移植受者中的3期研究中,一剂具有免疫原性,第二剂后一个月中和滴度适度升高。第二剂的额外获益在肾或肺移植参与者、移植后<2年者及接受麦考酚酸类者中更为明显,与本研究发现一致。在另一项评估另一种RSV疫苗(Abrysvo,Pfizer)的试验中,在包含实体器官移植受者、接受免疫调节剂治疗的自身免疫炎性疾病个体、晚期非小细胞肺癌患者或终末期肾病血液透析患者的广泛免疫功能受损队列中,单剂后一个月报告可变但有免疫原性的中和抗体应答;在该异质性人群中,第二剂在接种后一个月未进一步升高滴度。新兴真实世界有效性数据提示,单剂RSV疫苗可减少免疫功能受损人群RSV相关疾病和住院,尽管估计值常来自更广泛、异质性的免疫功能受损队列,且因结局、护理环境和人群特征而异。跨研究而言,发现提示免疫功能受损人群中的有效性通常与非免疫功能受损组相当,部分估计提示保护略有降低。一项近期使用行政索赔数据的大型美国回顾性队列研究(CLEAR-VE RSV)报告,adjuvanted RSVPreF3在≥60岁伴有免疫功能受损疾病的成人中对RSV相关住院的有效性为71.4%(95% CI:57.0,81.1),与总研究人群中观察到的估计值(75.6%[69.8,80.2])相当。类似地,一项较小的美国单中心检测阴性研究发现,adjuvanted RSVPreF3对免疫功能受损人群(占总体评估人群的16.2%)RSV相关下呼吸道感染住院具有高效力,估计值与总体和非免疫功能受损人群非常相似(总体人群:82.3%[95% CI:61.5,91.9];非免疫功能受损人群:81.1%[55.8,91.9];免疫功能受损人群:90.0%[11.6,98.9])。另一项近期使用美国退伍军人健康管理局数据的目标试验模拟评估了单剂RSV疫苗在两个RSV季节内对RSV感染的有效性,发现单剂RSV疫苗在≥60岁成人中提供初始强保护,但注意到有效性在18个月内下降,尤其在免疫功能受损人群中。来自更特定免疫功能受损人群的证据也在涌现;一项使用全国Epic Cosmos数据库的大型美国目标试验模拟发现,实体器官移植受者中接种RSV疫苗(随访期为2023年10月至2025年3月)与RSV感染、住院和全因死亡风险降低相关,各移植类型间发现总体一致。综上所述,本研究结果与既往免疫功能受损人群中RSV疫苗研究一致,表明免疫原性强,但应答幅度在各亚组间存在差异,反映该人群的异质性。本研究的一个关键优势是聚焦于中重度免疫功能受损的实体器官移植受者,提供稳健的免疫原性和安全性数据,有助于支持对其他免疫功能受损人群的解读。此外,本研究是首批评估免疫功能受损人群中两剂RSV疫苗方案的研究之一。研究设计支持重要的亚组分析,特别是区分接受含麦考酚酸与不含麦考酚酸免疫抑制方案的患者。免疫功能受损患者通常比免疫功能正常个体经历更快的疫苗诱导免疫消退;因此本研究至接种后12个月的长期随访提供了该高危人群中安全性和免疫应答持久性的重要数据。纳入同期非免疫功能受损组作为对照有助于确保各组跨地区和时间的RSV季节暴露相似,从而增强比较的同质性。总体而言,本试验发现为免疫功能受损人群RSV疫苗接种证据基础贡献了宝贵数据。本研究存在若干局限性。尽管研究为困难患者人群中的疫苗免疫原性提供了重要见解,但描述性研究设计、样本量(尤其特定亚组内)及混杂因素控制不完全可能影响结论强度。此外,细胞介导免疫原性亚组为非随机选择,限制了这些分析的比较和解读。更广泛而言,研究聚焦于免疫原性,认识到RSV特异性中和滴度和T细胞应答被视为保护性免疫的关键组成部分,而RSV疫苗尚无经验证的保护相关物。未来工作可探索特定免疫抑制剂类别组合是否对疫苗应答产生差异化影响,以及不同给药间隔是否影响免疫原性。此外,特定免疫功能受损亚人群中的有效性评估将支持风险分层并指导疫苗接种政策。 研究结论部分翻译如下:单剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3在接受维持免疫抑制治疗的肾或肺移植受者中具有免疫原性。在接受两剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3的移植受者中,第二剂后约一个月的中和滴度在数值上高于第一剂后,且与非免疫功能受损个体中观察到的范围相似。亚组分析显示,接受麦考酚酸类药物的个体单剂后应答尤其受到抑制;然而第二剂后,该亚组滴度与非免疫功能受损对照中观察到的范围相似。两种给药方案在移植受者中均引发RSVPreF3特异性细胞介导免疫应答,与对照中观察到的总体一致。体液和细胞介导免疫应答在完成单剂或两剂方案后下降,但持续至12个月。两种剂次的安全性特征均可接受。总体而言,研究结果支持adjuvanted RSVPreF3在免疫功能受损人群中具有有利的获益-风险特征。 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)等常见呼吸道病毒对免疫功能受损个体构成显著的发病和死亡风险。此类免疫功能受损状态包括原发性免疫缺陷、长期(移植后)免疫抑制治疗、血液系统恶性肿瘤或人类免疫缺陷病毒感染等,可增加个体对迁延性和更严重RSV疾病的易感性。超过三分之一的免疫功能受损RSV感染者可发生肺炎和住院。此外,受累个体常遗留长期后遗症;一项系统综述报告,近半数感染RSV的肺移植受者出现肺功能下降。该群体还面临RSV相关移植物并发症(急性细胞排斥、移植物功能障碍或慢性肺移植物功能障碍)的高风险。RSV相关死亡率相当可观;因RSV住院的造血干细胞移植受者中,全因死亡中位率达17.5%,成人骨髓移植受者中RSV相关汇总病死率为6.0%。成人RSV疾病的治疗选择在很大程度上仍以支持治疗为主,凸显了疫苗接种等预防策略对高危群体的重要性。然而,免疫功能受损人群的疫苗应答常常减弱,严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2(SARS-CoV-2)、流感及其他疫苗中均可见此现象。在移植受者中,特定免疫抑制方案尤其是麦考酚酸类化合物是免疫原性降低的关键因素。增加疫苗剂次可能有助于改善和维持保护。基于预融合F蛋白的疫苗代表RSV预防的重大进展。RSV F蛋白作为此类疫苗的抗原靶点,在RSV-A和RSV-B两种不同亚型间高度保守,两种亚型可共同流行,且常随地点和季节变化而消长。由于RSV-A和RSV-B共享该抗原,单价F蛋白疫苗可提供跨亚型保护。此外,F蛋白的预融合形式负责大部分中和抗体活性。AS01E佐剂化RSV预融合F蛋白疫苗(adjuvanted RSVPreF3,Arexvy,GSK)可预防成人RSV-A和RSV-B亚型所致疾病。在非免疫功能受损老年人的1/2期剂量选择研究中,adjuvanted RSVPreF3单剂即可引发稳健免疫应答,两个月后第二剂未观察到额外免疫原性获益,支持该人群采用单剂基础方案。adjuvanted RSVPreF3最初在美国和欧洲获批作为单剂疫苗用于≥60岁人群及50–59岁重度RSV疾病风险增加人群。此后适应证已扩展至美国≥18岁重度RSV疾病风险增加成人(2026年3月),以及欧洲所有≥18岁成人(2026年1月)。在≥60岁人群中,一剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3在三个RSV季节内对RSV相关下呼吸道疾病的累积效力为62.9%(97.5%置信区间[CI]:46.7,74.8),近期真实世界有效性研究通过显示单剂RSV疫苗接种后RSV相关住院减少而佐证了上述发现。在伴有增加重度RSV疾病风险的慢性疾病(如肺病、心血管疾病、糖尿病)的≥60岁人群中,疫苗效力仍保持较高水平,免疫原性与无此类疾病个体相当。在伴有或不伴有此类慢性疾病的50–59岁人群及伴有类似疾病的18–49岁人群中,adjuvanted RSVPreF3对RSV-A和RSV-B中和滴度的免疫原性非劣效于≥60岁人群。该疫苗在这些年龄组中显示出可接受的安全性特征。对于免疫功能受损个体,新兴真实世界数据和免疫原性研究提示基于预融合F蛋白的RSV疫苗可减少RSV相关住院并引发免疫应答。然而,该人群中现有证据仍然有限,常合并异质性患者群体,且多为观察性研究。本研究呈现了一项多国、多中心试验(NCT05921903)的结果,该试验评估了adjuvanted RSVPreF3在≥18岁接受维持免疫抑制方案的肺或肾移植受者中,单剂或间隔30–60天两剂方案后的免疫原性、反应原性和安全性。≥50岁非免疫功能受损个体作为单剂对照。鉴于免疫功能受损个体可能存在次优免疫应答,主要研究目标为评估移植受者第二剂后免疫应答是否高于第一剂后。次要目标为描述移植受者与对照组相比的安全性和免疫原性。研究还评估了疫苗在接受含麦考酚酸方案与不含麦考酚酸方案的移植受者中的免疫原性。参与者接种后随访12个月以评估长期免疫原性和安全性。研究共纳入两个人群:免疫功能受损个体和非免疫功能受损个体,随访至(末次)接种后12个月,跨越5至6个预定访视以评估免疫原性和安全性。免疫功能受损队列由≥18岁、移植后至少一年且接受维持治疗以预防同种异体移植物排斥的肺或肾移植受者组成。这些参与者按1:1随机接受一剂(1剂移植组,n=131)或间隔30–60天两剂(2剂移植组,n=130)adjuvanted ED60;RSV-B:1剂移植组5002.9 ED60,2剂移植组4834.7 ED60,非免疫功能受损组9125.2 ED60)。第4访视时,非免疫功能受损组GMT点估计值低于第3访视但仍高于基线(RSV-A:5707.0 ED60;RSV-B:6281.6 ED60);1剂移植组与第3访视范围相似(RSV-A:4184.7 ED60;RSV-B:4461.7 ED60);2剂移植组第二剂后GMT数值高于第3访视,与非免疫功能受损组范围相似(RSV-A:5377.9 ED60;RSV-B:5820.8 ED60)。所有组后期访视RSV-A和RSV-B中和GMT点估计值低于第4访视,但至末次接种后12个月仍高于基线。第6访视时,RSV-A GMT范围为1773.4–2517.4 ED60,RSV-B为2206.7–2886.5 ED60。组间比较显示,第一剂后1–2个月(第3访视),非免疫功能受损组相对于合并移植组的调整GMT比为RSV-A 1.63(95% CI:1.29,2.06),RSV-B 1.69(1.33,2.15),提示移植受者单剂后初始中和应答低于非免疫功能受损组。第4访视时,非免疫功能受损组相对于2剂移植组的调整GMT比为RSV-A 1.02(0.80,1.30),RSV-B 1.01(0.80,1.26),表明2剂移植组GMT点估计值与非免疫功能受损组范围相似;非免疫功能受损组相对于1剂移植组的调整GMT比为RSV-A 1.31(1.01,1.68),RSV-B 1.29(1.00,1.65),表明1剂移植组GMT点估计值低于非免疫功能受损组。随时间推移组间差异减弱。亚组分析显示,按移植亚型分层,肺和肾移植受者一剂和两剂后RSV-A和RSV-B GMT点估计值范围相似。按免疫抑制方案分层,未接受麦考酚酸类方案的移植受者(占23.4%)第一剂后初始RSV-A和RSV-B GMT与非免疫功能受损组范围相似,第二剂后GMT与第一剂后范围相似;接受麦考酚酸类方案的移植受者(占76.6%)第一剂后初始GMT点估计值低于非免疫功能受损组和未接受麦考酚酸类的移植受者,但该亚组2剂移植组第二剂后GMT高于第一剂后,与非免疫功能受损组第一剂后范围相似。细胞介导免疫原性方面,基线时各组RSVPreF3特异性表达≥2种激活标志物的CD4T细胞中位频率范围相同,为每百万CD4T细胞161.0至239.0。接种后所有组频率高于基线,至末次接种后12个月仍远高于基线,第6访视各组范围为每百万CD4T细胞507.0至1220.0。按移植类型分层,肺和肾移植受者RSVPreF3特异性CD4T细胞频率范围相似。接受麦考酚酸类化合物的移植参与者RSVPreF3特异性CD4T细胞应答似乎得以保留。未检测到RSVPreF3特异性CD8T细胞应答。反应原性和安全性方面,第一剂后7天内,1剂移植组80.2%、2剂移植组81.3%、非免疫功能受损组84.8%的参与者报告至少一种征集性事件;3级征集性事件分别报告于0.8%、3.9%和1.6%的参与者。第一剂后,至少一种征集性给药部位事件分别报告于73.3%、71.9%和76.8%的参与者,最常见为疼痛(分别为72.5%、71.9%和76.0%)。2剂移植组两名参与者报告3级征集性给药部位事件(一例疼痛,一例肿胀)。第一剂后,至少一种征集性全身事件分别报告于55.0%、51.6%和59.2%的参与者;移植组最常见为疲乏(1剂组31.3%,2剂组35.2%),非免疫功能受损组为肌痛(39.2%)。2剂移植组第二剂后7天内,77.7%的参与者报告至少一种征集性事件,2.5%报告至少一种3级征集性事件;至少一种征集性给药部位事件报告于68.6%的参与者,多为疼痛(67.8%);至少一种征集性全身事件报告于54.5%的参与者,最常见为疲乏(38.8%)。任何剂次后,各征集性事件类型中位持续时间≤3天(任何级别),除外2剂移植组第一剂后单次发热持续6天。接种后30天内报告的非征集性不良事件(AE)发生率和强度在各组和剂次间大致相当。移植受者中最常见系统器官分类(SOC)为感染和侵染;非免疫功能受损参与者中最常见SOC为呼吸、胸和纵隔疾病。第一剂后,研究者判定为疫苗相关的至少一种非征集性AE分别报告于1剂移植组3.1%、2剂移植组9.2%、非免疫功能受损组4.8%的参与者;第二剂后,2剂移植组7.4%的参与者报告至少一种研究者判定为疫苗相关的非征集性AE。至研究结束,严重不良事件(SAE)在移植组更频繁(1剂组22.9%,2剂组30.0%)高于非免疫功能受损组(3.2%)。移植组最常见SAE为肺炎。一例SAE(1剂移植组胃肠炎)被研究者判定为疫苗相关。2剂移植组报告一例3级SAE(过敏性休克),研究者判定与疫苗无关。报告六例死亡(均在移植组),均判定与疫苗无关。至研究结束,1剂移植组两名参与者(1.5%)、2剂移植组三名参与者(2.3%)、非免疫功能受损组两名参与者(1.6%)报告至少一种特殊关注不良事件(AESI),均判定与疫苗无关。研究中未报告妊娠。总计六名参与者因非征集性AE或SAE退出研究,均判定与疫苗无关。独立数据监查委员会未提出关切。讨论部分指出,免疫功能受损个体面临重度RSV结局风险增加,是疫苗接种的重要优先人群。RSV疫苗在免疫功能受损个体中的免疫原性数据及真实世界有效性证据正在积累,但多数证据来自包含多样化免疫功能受损亚组的广泛异质性队列。本研究呈现了adjuvanted RSVPreF3在接受维持免疫抑制方案的肺和肾移植受者中的免疫原性、反应原性和安全性,其中76.6%接受麦考酚酸类化合物。描述性免疫原性分析显示,单剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3可提高肺和肾移植受者的体液和细胞介导免疫应答,应答持续至接种后12个月。针对RSV-A和RSV-B亚型均产生强中和抗体应答,两个亚型在各时间点应答相似,证明跨RSV亚型一致且广泛反应性的免疫特征。然而,与非免疫功能受损对照相比,移植受者单剂后通常表现出更慢的诱导和更低的RSV-A和RSV-B中和滴度。间隔1–2个月第二剂后,移植受者滴度进一步升高,与非免疫功能受损个体范围相似。该应答模式主要在接收麦考酚酸类的移植受者中观察到,其单剂后初始滴度通常低于非免疫功能受损人群,但第二剂后达到相似范围。未接受麦考酚酸类的受者单剂后RSV-A/RSV-B滴度在所有时间点与非免疫功能受损组范围相似,第二剂未导致进一步升高。上述发现与免疫抑制人群中其他疫苗(流感、SARS-CoV-2、肺炎球菌等)的既往研究一致,这些研究将麦考酚酸确定为体液免疫原性降低的强预测因素。细胞介导免疫原性在每组小部分参与者中评估;总体而言,一剂或两剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3诱导的RSVPreF3特异性CD4T细胞应答在所有组中至研究结束仍高于基线。在该免疫功能受损人群中观察到的稳健且持续的体液和细胞免疫应答值得关注。AS01E佐剂与强而持久的CD4T细胞应答及高中和滴度相关,可能有助于在免疫抑制背景下观察到该免疫原性。两种给药方案的adjuvanted RSVPreF3均耐受良好,安全性特征可接受。大多数征集性事件为轻至中度且短暂,非征集性AE在各组间总体相当。移植受者SAE报告频率高于非免疫功能受损个体;移植组最常见SAE系统器官分类为感染和侵染,最常见SAE为肺炎,与该人群对重度呼吸道感染的已知易感性一致。一例SAE被研究者评估为疫苗相关(1剂移植组胃肠炎),由于患者炎症状态、潜在混杂因素及因果关系证据不足,申办方评估该事件与研究干预无关。目前免疫功能受损人群中RSV疫苗数据有限,且 largely 反映单剂评估。现有免疫原性数据在各研究间差异较大,可能反映研究规模、设计、基础疾病和免疫抑制方案的差异。一项在免疫功能受损成人(主要为实体器官移植受者)中的小型研究显示,单剂两种RSV疫苗之一(包括adjuvanted RSVPreF3)可引发中和抗体应答,但与本研究观察相似,较非免疫功能受损人群历史数据应答降低。一项在异基因造血干细胞移植和肺移植受者中的单中心干预性队列研究也注意到,单剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3后约一个月两种情况下体液免疫应答均适度增加。另一项在肺移植受者中的单中心回顾性队列研究报告,单剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3诱导的抗体应答持续高于基线至接种后六个月。评估免疫功能受损人群中两剂RSV疫苗接种策略的临床研究显示结果不一。在一项mRNA-1345 RSV疫苗(mRESVIA,Moderna)在肝、肾和肺移植受者中的3期研究中,一剂具有免疫原性,第二剂后一个月中和滴度适度升高。第二剂的额外获益在肾或肺移植参与者、移植后<2年者及接受麦考酚酸类者中更为明显,与本研究发现一致。在另一项评估另一种RSV疫苗(Abrysvo,Pfizer)的试验中,在包含实体器官移植受者、接受免疫调节剂治疗的自身免疫炎性疾病个体、晚期非小细胞肺癌患者或终末期肾病血液透析患者的广泛免疫功能受损队列中,单剂后一个月报告可变但有免疫原性的中和抗体应答;在该异质性人群中,第二剂在接种后一个月未进一步升高滴度。新兴真实世界有效性数据提示,单剂RSV疫苗可减少免疫功能受损人群RSV相关疾病和住院,尽管估计值常来自更广泛、异质性的免疫功能受损队列,且因结局、护理环境和人群特征而异。跨研究而言,发现提示免疫功能受损人群中的有效性通常与非免疫功能受损组相当,部分估计提示保护略有降低。一项近期使用行政索赔数据的大型美国回顾性队列研究(CLEAR-VE RSV)报告,adjuvanted RSVPreF3在≥60岁伴有免疫功能受损疾病的成人中对RSV相关住院的有效性为71.4%(95% CI:57.0,81.1),与总研究人群中观察到的估计值(75.6%[69.8,80.2])相当。类似地,一项较小的美国单中心检测阴性研究发现,adjuvanted RSVPreF3对免疫功能受损人群(占总体评估人群的16.2%)RSV相关下呼吸道感染住院具有高效力,估计值与总体和非免疫功能受损人群非常相似(总体人群:82.3%[95% CI:61.5,91.9];非免疫功能受损人群:81.1%[55.8,91.9];免疫功能受损人群:90.0%[11.6,98.9])。另一项近期使用美国退伍军人健康管理局数据的目标试验模拟评估了单剂RSV疫苗在两个RSV季节内对RSV感染的有效性,发现单剂RSV疫苗在≥60岁成人中提供初始强保护,但注意到有效性在18个月内下降,尤其在免疫功能受损人群中。来自更特定免疫功能受损人群的证据也在涌现;一项使用全国Epic Cosmos数据库的大型美国目标试验模拟发现,实体器官移植受者中接种RSV疫苗(随访期为2023年10月至2025年3月)与RSV感染、住院和全因死亡风险降低相关,各移植类型间发现总体一致。综上所述,本研究结果与既往免疫功能受损人群中RSV疫苗研究一致,表明免疫原性强,但应答幅度在各亚组间存在差异,反映该人群的异质性。本研究的一个关键优势是聚焦于中重度免疫功能受损的实体器官移植受者,提供稳健的免疫原性和安全性数据,有助于支持对其他免疫功能受损人群的解读。此外,本研究是首批评估免疫功能受损人群中两剂RSV疫苗方案的研究之一。研究设计支持重要的亚组分析,特别是区分接受含麦考酚酸与不含麦考酚酸免疫抑制方案的患者。免疫功能受损患者通常比免疫功能正常个体经历更快的疫苗诱导免疫消退;因此本研究至接种后12个月的长期随访提供了该高危人群中安全性和免疫应答持久性的重要数据。纳入同期非免疫功能受损组作为对照有助于确保各组跨地区和时间的RSV季节暴露相似,从而增强比较的同质性。总体而言,本试验发现为免疫功能受损人群RSV疫苗接种证据基础贡献了宝贵数据。本研究存在若干局限性。尽管研究为困难患者人群中的疫苗免疫原性提供了重要见解,但描述性研究设计、样本量(尤其特定亚组内)及混杂因素控制不完全可能影响结论强度。此外,细胞介导免疫原性亚组为非随机选择,限制了这些分析的比较和解读。更广泛而言,研究聚焦于免疫原性,认识到RSV特异性中和滴度和T细胞应答被视为保护性免疫的关键组成部分,而RSV疫苗尚无经验证的保护相关物。未来工作可探索特定免疫抑制剂类别组合是否对疫苗应答产生差异化影响,以及不同给药间隔是否影响免疫原性。此外,特定免疫功能受损亚人群中的有效性评估将支持风险分层并指导疫苗接种政策。研究结论部分翻译如下:单剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3在接受维持免疫抑制治疗的肾或肺移植受者中具有免疫原性。在接受两剂adjuvanted RSVPreF3的移植受者中,第二剂后约一个月的中和滴度在数值上高于第一剂后,且与非免疫功能受损个体中观察到的范围相似。亚组分析显示,接受麦考酚酸类药物的个体单剂后应答尤其受到抑制;然而第二剂后,该亚组滴度与非免疫功能受损对照中观察到的范围相似。两种给药方案在移植受者中均引发RSVPreF3特异性细胞介导免疫应答,与对照中观察到的总体一致。体液和细胞介导免疫应答在完成单剂或两剂方案后下降,但持续至12个月。两种剂次的安全性特征均可接受。总体而言,研究结果支持adjuvanted RSVPreF3在免疫功能受损人群中具有有利的获益-风险特征。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! 从2000到2026,27载全因有您;您的每一分支持,都给予我们无穷的动力! 公测期:打赏8元解锁30天免费阅读!

Larisa Savage, a certified nurse-midwife with Carle Health, said pregnancy changes how the immune system responds to illnesses like RSV, influenza and COVID-19. “During pregnancy, your immune system has to adapt,” Savage said. “When you’re exposed to those illnesses in the winter, your body can’t respond with maybe the same force that it once did.” One virus health care providers are watching closely is respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV. It is the leading cause of hospitalization for infants in the United States according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Savage said one way to help protect newborns is by getting the RSV vaccine during pregnancy. “The RSV vaccine is a way for us to protect newborn babies because it’s something pregnant women can get while they’re pregnant before the baby has arrived,” Savage said. “That way we’re giving baby some protection from something they most likely will be exposed to. We just want to limit those hospitalizations for those kiddos.” Beyond vaccination, Savage said families should take simple precautions during holiday gatherings, including washing their hands, staying home when they’re sick and respecting parents’ boundaries around newborns. She also encourages new parents to use a baby carrier during family gatherings, saying it can naturally discourage people from asking to hold the baby while still allowing loved ones to visit. Savage said parents shouldn’t feel guilty about limiting visits if it means protecting their newborn during cold and flu season. “It’s not worth it to go to a setting where people are not going to prioritize you or your newborn’s health,” Savage said. These findings were documented in a cross-sectional clinical study conducted at a tertiary care center in New Delhi, India. The investigation provides critical functional data on humoral and cellular immune parameters among aging individuals seeking care for non-acute, non-respiratory conditions. The research addresses a substantial gap in evidence concerning functional immunity to respiratory syncytial virus within low- and middle-income nations. While older adults suffering from underlying medical conditions are recognized to experience substantial morbidity from respiratory syncytial virus infections, the relationship connecting humoral antibody activity with cellular immune defenses has remained insufficiently characterized. To clarify these mechanisms, the investigators evaluated adults aged sixty years and older who presented to outpatient clinics or were admitted to inpatient wards for non-acute, non-respiratory illnesses. Discover more health Health Cancer treatment information Serological testing revealed that every enrolled participant across all evaluated age groups was seropositive for respiratory syncytial virus. When the research team quantified binding antibody levels directed against the viral fusion protein, they found that titers varied widely across individual subjects. However, statistical comparisons demonstrated that these binding antibody concentrations did not differ significantly by participant age or biological sex. In addition, the researchers observed a statistically significant positive correlation between binding immunoglobulin G levels and neutralizing antibody titers across the study population. Discover more Research assistant services Postdoc opportunities Research report templates Learn Engineering Despite possessing robust binding antibody concentrations, older individuals with chronic conditions exhibited marked deficiencies in functional antiviral activity. The overall magnitude of neutralizing antibody titers was lower in older adults with comorbidities when compared directly against healthy young adult controls. Furthermore, stratified analyses demonstrated that neutralizing capacity was significantly diminished in specific clinical subgroups, with significantly lower activity observed among older adults suffering from chronic liver disease (p = 0.009) and those diagnosed with malignant conditions (p = 0.04). To determine whether these specific comorbidities remained independently associated with impaired antiviral neutralization after controlling for other clinical variables, the team performed multivariable regression analysis. The multivariable model identified chronic liver disease as an independent predictor of decreased neutralization, with an adjusted odds ratio of 7.83. Malignancy was likewise independently associated with lower neutralizing titers, showing an adjusted odds ratio of 4.12. Furthermore, diabetes emerged as another significant independent contributor to reduced neutralizing activity, yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 2.98. In addition to humoral impairments, the study identified substantial deficits in cellular immune responses directed against the pathogen. Respiratory syncytial virus-specific T-cell activity was significantly lower in older adults than in the cohort of healthy young adults. When evaluated by interferon-gamma enzyme-linked immunospot assays, samples from older adults yielded a median response of only 8 spot-forming units per million cells, compared to a median of 68 spot-forming units per million cells in healthy young individuals, a difference that reached statistical significance at p = 0.0068. Following laboratory stimulation with a respiratory syncytial virus peptide pool, the majority of biological samples obtained from older adults failed to produce interleukin-2, interferon-gamma, or tumor necrosis factor-alpha in CD4-positive and CD8-positive T cells. These combined observations indicate that while older adults with comorbidities preserve binding antibodies against the respiratory syncytial virus fusion protein, they experience severe reductions in neutralizing antibody potency and virus-specific T-cell immunity. content_title: Merck Receives Positive EU CHMP Opinion to Expand Marketing Authorization for ENFLONSIA® (clesrovimab) to Include Children Up to 24 Months of Age Who Remain Vulnerable to Severe RSV Disease Through Their Second RSV Season
content: RAHWAY, N.J.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Nov 13, 2026-- Merck (NYSE: MRK), known as MSD outside of the United States and Canada, announced today that the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use (CHMP) of the European Medicines Agency (EMA) adopted a positive opinion recommending the approval of an expanded indication for ENFLONSIA ® (clesrovimab) to include prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) in children up to 24 months of age at increased risk for severe RSV disease through their second RSV season. The CHMP recommendation will now be reviewed by the European Commission (EC) for marketing authorization in the European Union (EU), Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, and a final decision is expected in the next two months. ENFLONSIA was first approved by the U.S. FDA in June 2025 and by the European Commission in April 2026 for the prevention of RSV LRTD in infants born during or entering their first RSV season. ENFLONSIA is the first and only preventive option against RSV LRTD administered to infants without the need for weight-based dosing. As previously announced, the FDA accepted a supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for ENFLONSIA to expand its indication to include prevention of RSV LRTD in children under two years of age at increased risk for severe RSV disease through their second RSV season and set a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA), or target action, date of March 22, 2027. "For some children, the risk of severe RSV does not end after their first RSV season and they remain at increased risk for serious cases of RSV-related bronchiolitis or pneumonia that can require hospitalization," said Dr. Macaya Douoguih, vice president, Therapeutic Area Head, Global Clinical Development, Merck Research Laboratories. "The positive CHMP opinion is an important step toward bringing ENFLONSIA to children in the European Union who remain at increased risk, helping protect them during their second RSV season." Certain children, including those born with chronic lung disease, congenital heart disease, or early or moderately preterm birth with certain risk conditions, remain vulnerable to severe RSV disease during their second RSV season. The CHMP opinion is supported by results from the Phase 3 SMART trial (MK-1654-007) ( NCT04938830 ), which were presented at RSVVW’26, the 9th conference of the Respiratory Syncytial Virus Foundation (ReSViNET), in February 2026, published in the New England Journal of Medicine in September 2025 (interim RSV season 1 results) and JAMA Pediatrics in July 2026 (full results). ENFLONSIA is approved in more than 55 countries worldwide, including the United States , Canada, China, Japan, and the European Union , for use in infants during their first RSV season. Regulatory filings are underway for approval in additional countries globally, as well as for the expansion of the indication to include eligible children under two years of age in the United States and countries where ENFLONSIA is already approved. About the Phase 3 SMART trial The SMART trial (MK-1654-007) ( NCT04938830 ) was a Phase 3, randomized, partially-blind, palivizumab-controlled, multicenter study to evaluate the safety, efficacy and pharmacokinetics of ENFLONSIA in infants and children at increased risk for severe RSV disease over two RSV seasons. The trial enrolled early (<29 weeks gestational age [GA]) or moderate preterm infants (≥29 to ≤35 weeks GA) and infants with chronic lung disease (CLD) of prematurity or congenital heart disease (CHD) of any GA. In RSV season 1, participants were randomized 1:1 to receive either a 105 mg dose of ENFLONSIA (n=502) or monthly palivizumab (n=501) by intramuscular (IM) injection. In RSV season 2, eligible participants (children under 2 years of age with CLD, CHD or early or moderate preterm birth with certain risk conditions) received an additional open-label 210 mg dose of ENFLONSIA by IM injection (n=276). Nearly all participants (99%) who received ENFLONSIA in RSV season 2 had CLD (n=229) or CHD (n=43). About RSV globally Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a contagious virus that causes widespread seasonal infections and can lead to serious respiratory conditions such as bronchiolitis and pneumonia. As a leading cause of hospitalization among infants globally, there is persisting unmet need for RSV preventive options for both healthy and high-risk infants during their first RSV season as well as for children at increased risk for severe RSV disease through their second RSV season. RSV season is the time of year when RSV infections are most common, usually occurring autumn through spring of the next year in temperate climates. Timing and severity in a given community or region can vary year to year. About ENFLONSIA ® (clesrovimab-cfor) in the U.S. ENFLONSIA is Merck’s FDA-approved extended half-life monoclonal antibody (mAb) indicated for passive immunization for the prevention of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) in newborns and infants who are born during or entering their first RSV season. ENFLONSIA is administered using the same dose regardless of weight (105 mg/0.7 mL in a prefilled syringe) and is designed to provide direct, rapid and durable protection through 5 months, a typical RSV season. For infants born during the RSV season, ENFLONSIA is to be administered within the first week of life. For infants born outside of the RSV season, ENFLONSIA should be administered shortly before the RSV season begins. For infants undergoing cardiac surgery with cardiopulmonary bypass during or entering their first RSV season, an additional 105 mg dose is recommended as soon as the infant is stable after surgery. ENFLONSIA has a 30-month shelf life. Selected Safety Information for ENFLONSIA ® (clesrovimab-cfor) in the U.S. Do not administer ENFLONSIA to infants with a history of serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, to any component of ENFLONSIA. Serious hypersensitivity reactions, including anaphylaxis, have been observed with other human immunoglobulin G1 (IgG1) monoclonal antibodies. If signs or symptoms of a clinically significant hypersensitivity reaction or anaphylaxis occur, initiate appropriate medications and/or supportive therapy. ENFLONSIA may interfere with some immunologically-based RSV diagnostic assays (i.e., rapid antigen tests) as observed in laboratory studies. Confirmation using a reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) assay is recommended when rapid antigen assay results are negative and clinical observations are consistent with RSV infection. The most common adverse reactions were injection-site erythema (4.5%), injection-site swelling (3.2%) and rash (2.3%). The multiplex real-time RT-PCR test qualitatively detects and differentiates influenza A, influenza B and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) RNA in anterior nasal swab specimens from individuals with signs and symptoms of respiratory tract infection. Influenza and RSV often circulate at the same time, and respiratory season can stretch lab capacity. Testing for all three viruses in a single run can help laboratories keep pace during those months. Results are intended as an aid in differential diagnosis, in conjunction with other clinical, epidemiologic and laboratory findings. "This is a defining moment for Molecular Designs," said Michael Clark, CEO of Molecular Designs. "Earning FDA clearance requires rigorous manufacturing, robust quality systems and scientific discipline, and our team built all three. With respiratory season underway, we're ready to support labs with a cleared, practical way to test for flu A, flu B and RSV in a single run." The SimplicityDx Panel FluA/FluB/RSV includes influenza A, influenza B, RSV, and an internal control. It is designed to work with Molecular Designs' Simplicity Dx Extraction products. The panel's breakaway format is designed to let labs use only the tests needed for each run with minimal pipetting. This can help reduce waste and simplify inventory management, which is especially useful for labs with staffing constraints or volumes that swing with respiratory season. The format also supports batch processing for higher-volume days. "Our goal was never just to add another respiratory test," said Dr. Greer Massey, Chief Scientific Officer of Molecular Designs. "We set out to design one around how clinical labs actually work, with quality and efficiency as priorities from the start. Every choice, from the assay format to the run controls, came from working alongside lab teams and listening to what they need day to day." The SimplicityDx Panel FluA/FluB/RSV is for prescription use only and for use in laboratories certified under CLIA to perform high-complexity tests. Laboratories interested in the panel can connect with a Molecular Designs representative at https://www.moleculardesigns.com/dx-respiratory. About Molecular Designs Molecular Designs was founded by physicians to make molecular testing simpler, easier to access and more cost-effective. Based in Birmingham, Alabama, the company develops and manufactures PCR-based assays, components, reagents and instrumentation under GMP and ISO 13485:2016 quality standards. Its portfolio includes the FDA-cleared SimplicityDx Panel FluA/FluB/RSV, along with products labeled for research use only (RUO), which are not for use in diagnostic procedures. For more information, visit moleculardesigns.com and follow Molecular Designs on LinkedIn. More babies will get sick this RSV season because of immunization access challenges Toronto parent Scarlett Jones writes of her struggle to get her child immunized against RSV, despite the virus being a major cause of hospitalization for otherwise healthy babies Scarlett Jones Nov 17, 2026 2:30 PM Share on SPACES Share by Email Share on Facebook Share on X Share on LinkedIn Print Share via Text Message Credit: Mufid Majnun via Unsplash Listen to this article 00:03:45 The following op-ed is by Toronto resident Scarlett Jones, a new parent and public policy professional. — As a new parent, I knew that RSV (respiratory syncytial virus) is a major cause of hospitalization for otherwise healthy babies. What I didn’t know was the effort it would take to get my child protected against it, despite the province now offering universal RSV immunization for infants under eight months. A common seasonal virus, RSV can easily overwhelm immature immune systems, quickly becoming dangerous to tiny airways. Thankfully, infants can now be protected from RSV either with an immunizing antibody shot or from a parental vaccine during pregnancy. And infant immunization is proving remarkably effective, with a recent study showing that it has cut RSV-related ICU admissions by an incredible 97 per cent, and has reduced emergency care and hospital admissions by nearly 80 per cent. Big numbers for the smallest among us. However, because immunization is seasonal, babies born outside of RSV season, like mine, don’t receive it in the hospital at birth and need to follow up for it in the fall. No healthcare provider ever told me this as fall approached. It wasn’t mentioned when I took my child in for their two or four-month vaccines. In fact, I was surprised to learn that my family doctor doesn’t even offer it. “Ask around,” they recommended. And so I did. Ten phone calls later, I had two options. First, an appointment at a city-run clinic in Etobicoke, a one-hour-plus bus-subway-bus ride away. Or, a late evening slot in 10 days time at a somewhat closer downtown clinic. Baby screaming in my lap, I groaned and made the appointment. Checking the taxi fare there, I groaned again. As I learned from my phone calls, many primary care providers and clinics in downtown Toronto are simply not stocking the RSV shot for infants, and their offices are unable to redirect patients to locations that are. Toronto Public Health’s website on RSV shots for infants has information on just the two city-run clinics —- one in Etobicoke and one in Scarborough. It also states, incorrectly, that these clinics only offer RSV immunization to infants six months and above. The difficulties I encountered trying to find an infant RSV shot in Toronto shouldn’t be acceptable for a public immunization program. And, while my child is now immunized, many will not be because of it. Toronto Public Health should be maintaining a list of walk-in clinics where caregivers can access immunization. If few primary care providers are actually offering this immunization, then Toronto Public Health should make this clear and open more city-run locations. Meanwhile, the province should be ensuring that family doctors across the region are offering the immunization and directing their patients in accordance with public health recommendations. This information should be easily accessible, widely available and actively promoted. New parents shouldn’t have to chase down accurate information on where to protect their child. A few days after making my appointment, I started getting Instagram ads for Infant RSV Immunization at a nearby clinic. The algorithm, albeit late, was giving me what my doctor’s office and Toronto Public Health should have been able to. Parenthood may be a learn-as-you-go endeavour. Following public health advice for your infant shouldn’t be. See symptoms, latest data Madison Scott New York Connect Team Nov. 13, 2026, 1:44 p.m. ET Hear this story Flu cases in New York have reached a total of over 30,000 for the 2026 season as of Nov. 7, according to the state Department of Health. State health officials are urging New Yorkers to get vaccinated against influenza and other respiratory viruses. On Oct. 26, state Health Commissioner Dr. James McDonald declared flu “prevalent” in New York. To help residents track respiratory illness trends, the state health department launched a Seasonal Respiratory Virus Dashboard. The dashboard tracks confirmed cases and hospitalizations for influenza, COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus, or RSV. Here's what to know about flu cases in New York for the week ending Nov. 7, along with flu symptoms and prevention. How many flu cases are in New York? The state's Seasonal Respiratory Virus Dashboard is updated weekly on Fridays and tracks confirmed cases and hospitalizations for flu, COVID-19 and RSV. For the week ending Nov. 7, New York reported 12,006 laboratory-confirmed flu cases and 871 hospitalizations. That was a 50% increase in cases from the previous week, which ended Oct. 31. The counties reporting the highest numbers of cases for the week ending Nov. 7 were Kings, Queens, New York, Bronx, Suffolk and Westchester. The next dashboard update will include data for the week ending Nov. 14. What are the symptoms of the flu? Flu symptoms typically develop within two to three days of exposure, according to the state health department. Most people experience mild illness and recover on their own within two weeks. Older adults, young children, pregnant women, nursing home residents and people with asthma, lung disease, heart disease, diabetes or obesity face a higher risk of flu complications. The New York State Department of Health lists these common flu symptoms: Body aches Chills Cough Fatigue Fever Headache Sore throat Stuffy nose People who develop symptoms or test positive for the flu should stay home and away from others, cover coughs and sneezes, and clean and disinfect surfaces, according to state guidance. They should contact a health care provider when necessary. How can you prevent the flu? Getting vaccinated is the most effective way to prevent flu infection and reduce the risk of severe illness and complications, according to the state health department. The flu vaccine is available to New Yorkers ages 2 and older at participating pharmacies without a prescription. Children as young as 6 months can receive the vaccine at a health care provider's office. The state also recommends these steps to help prevent the flu: Wash your hands frequently. Avoid people who are sick. Wear a mask in crowded places. Improve indoor air quality by opening windows when possible. — Madison Scott is a New York Connect reporter, covering entertainment, breaking and consumer news, and trending topics with a focus on stories that matter to readers across New York State.
